newsitem.title: USA: N.J. regains most jobs lost in recession -- study.
newsitem.headline: N.J. regains most jobs lost in recession -- study.

text.p: The New Jersey economy, hit hard by the 1990-91 recession, finally is seeing the light at the end of the tunnel, according to a new report.

A panel of Rutgers University economists meeting Thursday released a more optimistic prediction about job creation in a state that lost more than 260,000 jobs in the recession. New Jersey has regained all but 6,000 of them, said Nancy Mantell, director of the Rutgers Economic Advisory Service.
The report predicted the economy would generate 65,000 new jobs in 1997, up from the 40,000 predicted by the governor's economic advisory council earlier this year.

Already the state's unemployment rate has fallen from 6.2 percent throughout most of 1996 to 5.5 percent, ending years in which the state consistently posted jobless rates a full percent higher than the national jobless figure.
In June, New Jersey's economy produced 3.7 million non- farm jobs.

Moreover, growth in personal income is outpacing employment. New Jerseyans have averaged nearly five percent growth since the depth of the recession in 1991. That will reach 5.6 percent in the next few years, the R-Econ report said.
That is good news for Gov. Christie Whitman, who is running for a second term this year.
